def count_anagram_matches(s, u, k):
    """Count distinct rearrangements of s that match template u in exactly k places.

    A rearrangement of s is any string t obtained by permuting the characters
    of s; two rearrangements are the same iff they are equal as strings (each
    distinct string is counted once, no matter how many permutations of s's
    character copies produce it).  Position i (0-based) is a match if
    t[i] == u[i].

    Input domain:
      - s and u are strings over lowercase letters 'a'-'z' with
        1 <= len(s) == len(u) <= 200,
      - k is an int with 0 <= k <= len(s).

    Returns the exact count (a Python int; it may be astronomically large --
    no modulus is applied) of distinct rearrangements t of s whose number of
    matching positions against u is exactly k.  Returns 0 when no
    rearrangement achieves exactly k matches (e.g. k exceeds the maximum
    attainable number of matches, or the remaining positions cannot all be
    made mismatches).  The result is deterministic and exact; enumerating the
    up-to-200! rearrangements is hopeless, so an algebraic method is required.

    >>> count_anagram_matches("aab", "aab", 1)
    2
    >>> count_anagram_matches("abc", "cba", 1)
    3
    >>> count_anagram_matches("aabbbcc", "abcabca", 3)
    48
    """
